blocks.raw: <WikiExamTable rows={[{"heading":"Zoning Category","description":"Primary Function and Typical Regulations"},{"content":"Residential Zone","description":"Single-family homes, duplexes, or apartments. Height limits (usually 2–3 stories for detached; up to 10+ for condos). Lot size minimums; setback requirements. Parking: 1–2 spaces per unit."},{"content":"Commercial Zone","description":"Retail, offices, services. Built-in parking requirement. Restrict ground-floor housing only if city policy explicitly bans mixed-use. 24-hour activity permitted. Noise and signage limits."},{"content":"Industrial Zone","description":"Manufacturing, warehousing, bulk storage. Usually surrounded by buffer zones. Setback from residential zones (often 50–100m). Truck traffic, waste discharge regulated. Height limits vary by facility type."},{"content":"Mixed-Use Zone (Horizontal)","description":"Residential and commercial on same lot. Common in urban renewal. Enables walkable districts. Requires clear separation (commercial on ground floor, residential above or adjacent)."},{"content":"Institutional Zone","description":"Government buildings, schools, health facilities, religious buildings. Often granted height exemptions. Parking and assembly space requirements. Not typically revenue-generating; focused on public service."},{"content":"Agricultural Zone","description":"Farming, fishponds, forestry, tree nurseries. Found at city periphery. Often conflict-prone: developers seek to rezone; environmental advocates resist. Minimum lot sizes (typically 2–5 hectares for farm operations)."}]} />

blocks.raw: <Tip>Zoning adoption = Sanggunian legislative function (not Planning Office, not Mayor alone). Zoning ordinance must align with CLUP. Use designations are enforceable rules with numeric limits (height, setback, lot size).</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Thinking the Planning Office 'approves' the zoning ordinance — it drafts it; the Sanggunian adopts it","Confusing zoning (legal use category) with land subdivision (physical division into lots) — zoning applies to both raw land and already-subdivided areas","Believing a Mayor can veto the zoning ordinance — the Mayor signs it but the Sanggunian passes it; veto is extremely rare","Assuming 'mixed-use' automatically includes residential — mixed-use must be explicitly permitted in the zoning code; many commercial zones exclude residential entirely"]} />
